mainTopic: Does the ציץ make an impure offering acceptable when something was done on purpose? The גמרא gives four ways to settle two ברייתות that disagree.
overview: An earlier ברייתא ruled that in some cases an impure offering is 'not accepted', but a second ברייתא says the ציץ makes impure blood, meat and fat acceptable even when done on purpose. רב יוסף answers that the lenient ברייתא is רבי יוסי, who does not penalize deliberate wrongdoing, as seen with תרומה. The גמרא objects that רבי יוסי holds the ציץ does not work for eaten parts, and tries to save the answer by reversing the names. רב ששת rejects the reversal with a long ברייתא about eating קדשים while impure: it holds that sprinkling does not work for meat that left the courtyard, which is רבי אליעזר's view, and it uses the ציץ for eaten parts. So רב חסדא answers instead that the lenient ברייתא is רבי אליעזר, who also does not penalize, even for קדשים. Finally רבינא and רב שילא each split the cases differently: one says only sprinkling on purpose ruins the offering, and the other says only making it impure on purpose does.

steps.title: End of the earlier teaching: the offering is not accepted
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of an earlier ברייתא: in the case being discussed, the offering is not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of a ברייתא that began before this section. It ended by saying that in a certain case the offering is not accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That earlier ברייתא listed cases where the ציץ does not fix an offering whose blood became impure. These closing words matter because the very next step contrasts them with a different ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: was accepted, meaning the offering counts and does its job
was not accepted, meaning the offering does not count

phrases.english: It is not accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the earlier ברייתא's case, the offering is not accepted.

steps.title: A second teaching says the frontplate works even for deliberate impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא saying the ציץ makes impure blood, meat and fat acceptable in every case, even if done on purpose. This clashes with the earlier ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: For what does the ציץ bring acceptance? For blood, meat and fat that became impure, whether by mistake or on purpose, whether forced or willingly, whether for a private offering or a communal one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets one ברייתא against another. This one says the ציץ works even when the impurity happened on purpose, which the earlier ברייתא denied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא said impure blood sprinkled on purpose is not accepted. This ברייתא says 'בין בשוגג בין במזיד', meaning even on purpose it is accepted, and it explicitly includes a private (יחיד) offering. So the two ברייתות cannot both be right as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: and they pointed out a contradiction between two sources
the golden frontplate worn by the כהן גדול
brings acceptance, makes the offering valid despite impurity
by mistake / on purpose
forced by circumstances / willingly
a private person's offering / the community's offering

steps.confusionAlert: The ציץ does not make the impure meat permitted to eat. It only makes the offering count, so the owner has fulfilled his obligation.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
For what does the frontplate effect acceptance?
For the blood and for the flesh
and for the fat that became impure,
whether unwittingly or intentionally,
whether under duress or willingly,
whether for an individual or for the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the ruling of the ברייתא that just ended.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier ברייתא's rule that impure blood sprinkled on purpose is not accepted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא says the ציץ works even במזיד and even for a יחיד, which directly conflicts with it.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the two teachings follow different opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the ברייתא allowing even deliberate cases follows רבי יוסי, and the stricter one follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is not a problem. This one is רבי יוסי, and that one is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the contradiction by assigning each ברייתא to a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתות do not contradict each other because they come from two sides of a dispute. The lenient ברייתא (even במזיד) is רבי יוסי's view. The strict ברייתא (במזיד not accepted) is the רבנן's view. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not a difficulty
this one ... that one, assigning each source to a different view

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is not difficult;
this is Rabbi Yosei, that is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא saying 'even on purpose' is רבי יוסי. The one saying 'on purpose is not accepted' is the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the sources to different תנאים (מחלוקת תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to express one view, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They reflect a dispute: the רבנן penalize deliberate wrongdoing, and רבי יוסי does not.

steps.title: Proof from separating תרומה from impure produce
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא showing that the רבנן penalize someone who acts on purpose, while רבי יוסי does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: You may not separate תרומה from impure produce for pure produce. If he did it by mistake, his תרומה counts. If on purpose, it does not count. רבי יוסי says: Whether by mistake or on purpose, his תרומה counts.
steps.whatsHappening: This ברייתא backs up רב יוסף's answer. It shows a real dispute about whether a deliberate wrongdoer is penalized.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן split between שוגג and מזיד: on purpose, the תרומה does not count, as a penalty. רבי יוסי makes no split. This matches the pattern of the two ברייתות about the ציץ: one splits between mistake and on purpose, and the other says 'whether by mistake or on purpose'.

keyTerms.meaning: the portion of produce given to a כהן
we separate תרומה
ritually impure / ritually pure

phrases.english: As it is taught: One may not separate teruma
from the impure for the pure,
phrases.notes: He means taking תרומה from impure produce to cover produce that is pure.

phrases.english: and if he separated unwittingly, his teruma is teruma,
intentionally, his teruma is not teruma.
Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּשׁוֹגֵג בֵּין בְּמֵזִיד – תְּרוּמָתוֹ תְּרוּמָה.
phrases.english: whether unwittingly or intentionally, his teruma is teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין תּוֹרְמִין מִן הַטָּמֵא עַל הַטָּהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רב יוסף's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי does not penalize deliberate action while the רבנן do.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on separating תרומה from impure produce for pure produce.

steps.title: Not penalizing is not the same as the frontplate working for eaten parts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. Fine, רבי יוסי does not penalize. But who says he holds the ציץ works for the eaten parts of an offering at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Say you heard that רבי יוסי does not penalize. Did you hear from him that the ציץ brings acceptance for the eaten parts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's answer. The proof only shows רבי יוסי is lenient about penalties, not that he agrees with everything in the lenient ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lenient ברייתא also says the ציץ works for impure 'flesh', which is a part that gets eaten. For רב יוסף's answer to work, רבי יוסי would have to agree to that too. The תרומה proof says nothing about the ציץ and eaten parts.

keyTerms.meaning: penalizes, imposes a קנס (a rabbinic penalty)
the parts of an offering that are eaten, such as the meat
granted that you heard him say this much

phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabbi Yosei hold
that he does not penalize;
that the frontplate effects acceptance for eaten portions,
did you hear him say that?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי דְּלָא קָנֵיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof from step 4 and the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the lenient ברייתא follows רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תרומה source only proves רבי יוסי does not penalize. It does not prove he holds the ציץ works for eaten parts, which the lenient ברייתא also teaches.

steps.title: רבי יוסי actually holds the frontplate does not work for eaten parts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי יוסי says outright that the ציץ does not work for eaten parts, against רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is taught: רבי אליעזר says: The ציץ brings acceptance for eaten parts. רבי יוסי says: The ציץ does not bring acceptance for eaten parts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its objection with a ברייתא. רבי יוסי explicitly disagrees with the idea that the ציץ works for eaten parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lenient ברייתא includes 'flesh', which is eaten. But רבי יוסי holds the ציץ does not help for eaten parts. So the lenient ברייתא cannot be רבי יוסי, and רב יוסף's answer looks broken.

keyTerms.meaning: the frontplate does not bring acceptance for impure eaten parts
a dispute between sages

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף tied the lenient ברייתא to רבי יוסי. But רבי יוסי rejects the ציץ working for eaten parts, which that ברייתא includes, so the answer is now under serious pressure.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The frontplate effects acceptance for eaten portions;
Rabbi Yosei says:
The frontplate does not effect acceptance for eaten portions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source that makes the objection in step 5 hard to answer.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי does not hold the ציץ works for eaten parts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא recording the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Reverse the two opinions
steps.stepSummary: To save רב יוסף's answer, the גמרא flips the opinions. Now רבי אליעזר says the ציץ does not work for eaten parts, and רבי יוסי says it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it: רבי אליעזר says the ציץ does not make eaten parts acceptable. רבי יוסי says the ציץ does make eaten parts acceptable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Step 6 by switching which sage holds which view in that ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed רבי יוסי saying the ציץ does not work for eaten parts. That would knock out רב יוסף's claim that the lenient ברייתא follows רבי יוסי. By reversing the names, רבי יוסי now holds the ציץ does work for eaten parts, so רב יוסף's answer can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it: switch which sage says which opinion.
The golden plate worn on the כהן גדול's forehead.
Makes a קרבן acceptable even though something impure is involved.
The eaten parts of a קרבן, such as the meat.

steps.confusionAlert: Nothing in the הלכה itself changes here. The גמרא is only switching which name goes with which opinion.

phrases.english: Reverse [the opinions]:
phrases.notes: He means: switch the names in the ברייתא from Step 6.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵין הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה עַל אֲכִילוֹת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: the frontplate does not effect acceptance for eaten parts,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה עַל אֲכִילוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: the frontplate does effect acceptance for eaten parts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב יוסף's answer against the challenge in Step 6 by reversing the attributions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי holds the ציץ does not work for eaten parts, so the lenient ברייתא cannot follow him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The names are switched, so רבי יוסי holds the ציץ does work for eaten parts and רב יוסף's answer survives.

steps.title: רב ששת asks whether the opinions can really be reversed
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת challenges the reversal. He starts quoting a ברייתא that asks whether someone who eats sacrificial meat while impure, before the blood was thrown, is liable for eating while impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objects: Can you really reverse it? But a ברייתא teaches: I might have thought that if someone eats sacrificial meat while impure before the blood is thrown, he is liable for eating while impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks the reversal and begins to bring a ברייתא as his source. The ברייתא opens with a 'you might have thought' question, so the גמרא is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת will argue that רבי אליעזר cannot hold the ציץ fails for eaten parts. His tool is a ברייתא about eating קדשים while impure before זריקת דמים. Here the ברייתא only raises the possibility that such a person is liable; the answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it: a strong challenge from a sage.
Throwing the blood of the קרבן on the מזבח. This is what permits the meat to be eaten.
Ritual impurity. Eating קדשים while impure carries a severe punishment.
'You might have thought': opens a possibility that the ברייתא will then reject.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet objects to this:
And are you able to reverse it?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל בָּשָׂר שֶׁנִּטְמָא לִפְנֵי זְרִיקַת דָּמִים
phrases.english: One might think that [eating] meat while impure before the sprinkling of the blood
phrases.notes: The case is a person who is impure eating the meat, as the פסוקים in the next step show.

phrases.english: would make one liable for it due to impurity?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: וּמִי מָצֵית אָפְכַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reversal proposed in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reversal that has רבי אליעזר saying the ציץ does not work for eaten parts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא holds that sprinkling does not work for יוצא, which is רבי אליעזר's known view. The same ברייתא uses the ציץ to make impure meat count for eating. So רבי אליעזר holds the ציץ works for eaten parts, and the reversal cannot stand. Step 20 completes this argument.

steps.title: Liability applies only to meat already permitted to pure people
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from two neighboring פסוקים that you are liable for eating while impure only if the meat is already permitted to pure people. Before the blood is thrown, it is not permitted, so there is no liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Everyone who is pure may eat the meat,' and right after: 'But the soul that eats meat of the שלמים offering, which belongs to ה׳, with his impurity upon him, shall be cut off.' Meat that is permitted to pure people brings liability for impurity. Meat that is not permitted to pure people does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question by placing two פסוקים side by side. This is the material רב ששת will use for his challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק about pure people eating comes right before the punishment for impure eating, the punishment applies only to meat that pure people may eat. Before זריקת דמים, no one may eat the meat, so an impure person who eats it then is not liable for eating while impure. The rule is: liability for טומאה depends on the meat being already permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches: introduces the verse that settles the question.
A peace offering, whose meat is eaten by the owners.
Shall be cut off: the punishment of כרת.
Already permitted to pure people: the meat is ready to be eaten.

steps.whatToRemember: Someone who eats קדשים while impure is liable only if the meat was already permitted to pure people. Before זריקת דמים, there is no such liability.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule about when meat counts as permitted is what רב ששת will use to attack the reversal of רבי אליעזר's opinion.

phrases.english: The verse states: "Everyone who is pure may eat the meat,"
"But the soul that eats meat
of the peace offering that belongs to the Lord,
with his impurity upon him, shall be cut off."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:20. It comes right after the first פסוק, and that closeness is the whole point.

phrases.english: That which is permitted to pure people:
one is liable for it due to impurity,
and that which is not permitted to pure people:
one is not liable for it due to impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that רב ששת began quoting in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that liability for eating while impure applies only to meat already permitted to pure people.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two neighboring פסוקים, ויקרא 7:19-20, as read in the ברייתא.

steps.title: Maybe any meat pure people cannot eat is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests another way to read the rule from Step 9. Perhaps any meat that pure people may not eat, such as לן and יוצא, carries no liability for eating it while impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe the rule means only this: meat that pure people may eat makes an impure eater liable, and meat that pure people may not eat does not. Then I would exclude meat left overnight and meat that went out of the עזרה, since pure people may not eat them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tests its own rule by reading it more broadly. If the rule is taken literally, it would also exempt meat that became forbidden after the blood was already thrown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 used the rule 'only meat permitted to pure people' to exempt meat before the blood was thrown. Here the ברייתא points out that לן and יוצא are also forbidden to pure people, even though their blood was already thrown. Read literally, the rule would exempt them too, and the ברייתא is unsure whether that is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or perhaps it means only…', a formula that raises another way to read a פסוק
Meat that pure people are allowed to eat
Liable (כרת) for eating קדשים while impure
Sacrificial meat left past its time overnight, which makes it forbidden
Sacrificial meat taken out of its permitted area, which makes it forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the ברייתא's final view. It is a possible reading that the next step will reject.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it means only this:
if it is eaten by pure people,
one is liable for it because of impurity,
and if it is not eaten by pure people,
one is not liable for it because of impurity.
Then I would exclude meat left overnight
phrases.notes: In other words, I would say an impure person who eats it is not liable.

phrases.english: and meat that went out,
since pure people may not eat them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how far the rule from Step 9 reaches
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that liability applies only to meat permitted to pure people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read literally, the rule would also exempt לן and יוצא, which were permitted after the blood was thrown but later became forbidden.

steps.title: The words 'that belong to ה׳' include them
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says ״אֲשֶׁר לַה׳״. This extra wording includes לן and יוצא, so an impure person who eats them is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק says: 'that belong to ה׳.' This includes them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the doubt from Step 10 with an extra phrase in the פסוק. The phrase widens the rule so that it covers לן and יוצא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״אֲשֶׁר לַה׳״ show that the איסור covers meat that once belonged to ה׳ as a valid offering, even if it later became forbidden. So the rule 'permitted to pure people' only excludes meat before the blood is thrown. It does not exclude meat that was permitted and later became forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The פסוק teaches', introducing proof from a פסוק
'That belong to ה׳', the words from the פסוק used to include more cases
'It included', meaning the פסוק widens the rule

phrases.english: Therefore the פסוק says: 'that belong to ה׳'
this included them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the broad reading raised in Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Derivation from an extra phrase that widens the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לן and יוצא carry no liability for eating while impure, since pure people may not eat them
steps.terutzMaskana: ״אֲשֶׁר לַה׳״ includes לן and יוצא, so an impure person who eats them is liable

steps.title: Should פיגול and נותר also be included?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the פסוק widens the rule, the ברייתא asks whether it also covers פיגול and נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could it be that I include פיגול meat and נותר meat too?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא checks how far the widening from Step 11 goes. It asks whether it also includes פיגול and נותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ״אֲשֶׁר לַה׳״ includes forbidden meat like לן and יוצא, maybe it includes every forbidden kind of sacrificial meat. פיגול and נותר are the next cases to test.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think', introducing a possible but wrong conclusion
Include in the rule
An offering made invalid by an intent to eat it or offer it after its proper time
Sacrificial meat left past its time to be eaten

phrases.english: One might think that I include
פיגול meats and נותר meats?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אֶת הַפִּיגּוּלִין וְאֶת הַנּוֹתָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the limits of the widening from Step 11
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If forbidden meats like לן are included, maybe פיגול and נותר are included as well.

steps.title: נותר is the same as לן, so the question is reworded
steps.stepSummary: The wording of the question is challenged, since נותר is the same as לן, which was already included. So the question is reworded: should פיגול be included, the way נותר is?
steps.simpleTranslation: נותר is the same as meat left overnight! Rather, the question is: should פיגול also be included, like נותר?
steps.whatsHappening: The question in Step 12 is challenged because it asks about something already settled. It is then fixed so that it only asks about פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat left overnight is exactly what נותר is, and Step 11 already included it. So asking about נותר makes no sense. The real question is whether פיגול is included the same way נותר is.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That is the same as'
'Rather', introducing the corrected version
'Like נותר meats', meaning the same way נותר is included

phrases.english: But נותר meats are the same as meat left overnight!
phrases.notes: That case was already included back in Step 11.

phrases.english: Rather, read: should even פיגול meats be included, like נותר meats?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges and fixes the wording of the question in Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'and נותר meats' in the question of Step 12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נותר is the same as לן, which was already included, so there is nothing to ask about it.

steps.title: 'From the peace offering' excludes פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says ״מִזֶּבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״. The word 'from' narrows the rule and excludes פיגול, so an impure person who eats פיגול is not liable for eating while impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the פסוק says: 'from the peace offering.' This excludes פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the reworded question with another phrase in the פסוק. This phrase limits the rule so that פיגול is not included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אֲשֶׁר לַה׳״ widened the rule to include לן and יוצא. ״מִזֶּבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״ narrows it back down to leave out פיגול. The ברייתא does not yet explain why פיגול goes on the excluded side; Step 16 gives the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From the peace offering', the phrase used to narrow the rule
'It excluded', meaning the פסוק narrows the rule

steps.whatToRemember: Eating while impure: before the blood is thrown, no liability. For לן and יוצא, liable (from ״אֲשֶׁר לַה׳״). For פיגול, not liable (from ״מִזֶּבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״).
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the material רב ששת uses to challenge the reversed opinions from Step 7. Knowing exactly what is included and excluded here is needed to follow his challenge.

phrases.english: Therefore the פסוק says: 'from the peace offering'
this excluded פיגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reworded question from Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Derivation from a phrase that narrows the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פיגול is included in the liability, like נותר
steps.terutzMaskana: ״מִזֶּבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים״ excludes פיגול, so an impure person who eats it is not liable

steps.title: Why include these and exclude those?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the extra wording includes לן and יוצא but the word 'from' excludes פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what reason do you have to include these (לן and יוצא) and to exclude those (פיגול)?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks what the reason is for sorting the cases this way. This sets up the next step, where it gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק gave us one word that widens the rule and one word that narrows it. But the פסוק did not say which case goes on which side. So the ברייתא asks why לן and יוצא go on the 'include' side and פיגול goes on the 'exclude' side.

keyTerms.meaning: What reason did you see? This asks for the logic behind a choice.
To include
To exclude

phrases.english: And what did you see to include these
phrases.notes: 'These' means לן and יוצא, which were included in Step 11.

phrases.english: and to exclude those?
phrases.notes: 'Those' means פיגול, which was excluded in Step 14.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת אֶת אֵלּוּ וּלְהוֹצִיא אֶת אֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the include/exclude split set up in Steps 11 and 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why are לן and יוצא the included cases while פיגול is the excluded one, and not the other way around?

steps.title: The difference is a period of fitness
steps.stepSummary: לן and יוצא had a time when they were fit, so they are included. פיגול never had one, so it is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the פסוק both included and excluded, you should say: I include these, which had a time when they were fit, and I exclude those, which never had a time when they were fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its reason. Meat that was once fit and later became disqualified (לן, יוצא) is included. פיגול, which was never fit, is excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לן and יוצא were fine after the blood was sprinkled. Only later did they become disqualified, by staying overnight or leaving the courtyard. פיגול is ruined by a wrong intention during the service itself, so it was never fit for even a moment. Whether there was a שעת הכושר decides whether eating it while impure brings liability.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק included and also excluded
A period of fitness, a time when the meat was fit to eat

steps.whatToRemember: לן and יוצא had a שעת הכושר, so eating them while impure brings liability. פיגול never had a שעת הכושר, so it does not.

phrases.english: After the verse included and excluded,
you should say: I include these
which had a period of fitness,
and I exclude those
which did not have a period of fitness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dividing line is שעת הכושר. Meat that was once fit is included, and meat that was never fit is excluded.

steps.title: Meat that became impure before the sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: If the rule depends on a period of fitness, why is someone liable for eating meat that became impure before the blood was sprinkled?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: meat that became impure before the blood was sprinkled, and a person ate it after the blood was sprinkled, why is he liable for it because of impurity?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a challenge to the rule it just gave. It brings a case where the meat seems never to have been fit, yet eating it while impure brings liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Impure meat may not be eaten, so meat that became impure before the sprinkling was already unfit when the blood was sprinkled. By the rule of Step 16, it should be like פיגול, with no liability. Yet the halacha is that an impure person who eats it is liable, so the rule seems to have a hole.

keyTerms.meaning: The sprinkling of the blood on the מזבח, which makes the meat permitted to eat
And if you will say. This introduces a possible objection.

phrases.english: And if you say: meat that became impure
before the sprinkling of the blood
and he ate it after the sprinkling of the blood,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם טוּמְאָה?
phrases.english: for what reason is one liable for it due to impurity?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תֹּאמַר: בָּשָׂר שֶׁנִּטְמָא לִפְנֵי זְרִיקַת דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the שעת הכושר rule of Step 16 with a counterexample.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only meat with a שעת הכושר brings liability for eating while impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Meat that became impure before the sprinkling was never fit, yet one is liable for eating it while impure. That seems to contradict the rule.

steps.title: The ציץ makes it acceptable
steps.stepSummary: The ציץ makes the offering acceptable despite the impurity, so the sprinkling counts and the meat is treated as having been fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the ציץ effects acceptance.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge. The ציץ, the כהן גדול's golden frontplate, makes up for the impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ makes the offering acceptable even though it is impure, so the sprinkling of the blood is valid. Because the sprinkling worked, the meat counts as having had a שעת הכושר, and the rule of Step 16 still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden frontplate worn by the כהן גדול
Effects acceptance, makes the offering acceptable despite a problem

phrases.english: Because the frontplate effects acceptance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces an outside factor, the ציץ, that turns the case into one that does have a period of fitness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Meat that became impure before the sprinkling was never fit, so there should be no liability.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ציץ makes the sprinkling valid despite the impurity, so the meat counts as having had a שעת הכושר and liability applies.

steps.title: Impurity yes, leaving the courtyard no
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the ברייתא that the ציץ helps for impurity but not for meat that left the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it became impure, yes. If it left the courtyard, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finished, and now the גמרא draws an inference from it. This is the first half of a proof that the next step completes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used the ציץ only to solve the case of impurity. So the ציץ fixes impurity, but meat that left the courtyard before the sprinkling stays without a period of fitness. That means the ברייתא holds that sprinkling does not work for יוצא, and the next step uses this to identify who wrote it.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes / no. A short way of saying 'this case works, that case does not'.

steps.confusionAlert: Earlier, יוצא was included because it left the courtyard after the sprinkling. Here the point is about meat that left before the sprinkling. The ציץ does not fix that.

phrases.english: Became impure: yes,
left the courtyard: no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא's answer in Step 18.
steps.raayaObject: The view of the ברייתא about whether sprinkling works for יוצא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא uses the ציץ only for impurity, not for יוצא

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, so the ציץ helps for eating
steps.stepSummary: Only רבי אליעזר holds that sprinkling does not work for יוצא. Since this ברייתא is his, he holds that the ציץ makes the eaten parts acceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom have you heard who says that sprinkling does not work for meat that left the courtyard? רבי אליעזר. And this ברייתא teaches that the ציץ effects acceptance for the parts that are eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת finishes his challenge. The ברייתא is רבי אליעזר's, and it says the ציץ works for eaten parts, so the reversal of Step 7 cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 showed that the ברייתא holds sprinkling does not work for יוצא, and that is the known view of רבי אליעזר. The same ברייתא uses the ציץ to fix impure meat that is eaten, so רבי אליעזר holds ציץ מרצה על אכילות, just as the original wording in Step 6 said. The reversal fails, רבי יוסי really holds the ציץ does not work for eaten parts, and רב יוסף's answer falls.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood does not work for meat that has left the courtyard
The ציץ effects acceptance for the parts of the offering that are eaten

steps.whatToRemember: This ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, and it shows that he holds the ציץ effects acceptance for impure meat that is eaten (ציץ מרצה על אכילות).
steps.whyThisMatters: It knocks out the reversal of Step 7. רבי יוסי is back to holding that the ציץ does not work for eaten parts, so רב יוסף's answer collapses. That is why רב חסדא gives a new answer in the next step.

phrases.english: Whom have you heard who says:
'Sprinkling is not effective for meat that left'?
Rabbi Eliezer,
and it teaches that the frontplate effects acceptance for eaten portions.
phrases.notes: 'It' is this same ברייתא, which turns out to be רבי אליעזר's.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָמַר: אֵין זְרִיקָה מוֹעֶלֶת לַיּוֹצֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the inference of Step 19 by naming the author of the ברייתא. This finishes רב ששת's challenge from Step 8 and refutes the reversal of Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר's view on whether the ציץ effects acceptance for eaten portions
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, which follows רבי אליעזר because it holds אין זריקה מועלת ליוצא, and which uses the ציץ for impure meat that is eaten

steps.title: רב חסדא: the two ברייתות follow different opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא settles the contradiction by assigning the lenient ברייתא to רבי אליעזר and the strict one to the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: there is no problem. This ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, and that ברייתא follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the reversal failed, רב יוסף's answer (that the lenient ברייתא is רבי יוסי) is dropped. רב חסדא brings a new answer: each ברייתא follows a different תנא, but the lenient one is רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that accepts the offering even when it was done on purpose follows רבי אליעזר. We just saw that he holds the ציץ makes the eaten parts acceptable. The ברייתא that accepts it only when it was a mistake follows the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
This one ... that one (pointing to two sources)
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chisda said
It is not difficult
This one is Rabbi Eliezer
that one is the Rabbis

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 20 to settle the contradiction between the ברייתות
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא (מחלוקת)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות must follow one opinion, so they contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient ברייתא is רבי אליעזר and the strict ברייתא is the רבנן

steps.title: Does רבי אליעזר also not penalize someone who acted on purpose?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. Knowing that the ציץ works for the eaten parts in רבי אליעזר's view does not prove that he drops the penalty for someone who acted on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, you heard that רבי אליעזר holds the ציץ makes the eaten parts acceptable. But did you ever hear him say that we do not penalize someone who acted on purpose?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a gap in רב חסדא's answer. Step 20 proved only one point about רבי אליעזר, but the lenient ברייתא needs two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lenient ברייתא says the offering is accepted even when the impurity was caused on purpose. That needs two things. First, the ציץ must work. Second, the חכמים must not fine (קנס) a person who acted on purpose. Step 20 only proved the first.

keyTerms.meaning: The ציץ (gold plate on the כהן גדול's forehead) makes the offering acceptable
The parts of the offering that are eaten
Penalizes; the חכמים impose a fine (קנס) on wrongdoing
Say that you heard him (say only this much); used to limit a proof

phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabbi Eliezer holds
that the ציץ makes acceptable the parts to be eaten
that he does not penalize — did you hear that from him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דִּמְרַצֵּה צִיץ עַל אֲכִילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer from step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the lenient ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Proving that the ציץ works does not prove that there is no fine for acting on purpose

steps.title: Yes: רבי אליעזר does not penalize, as we see with תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר, like רבי יוסי, does not penalize. It brings a ברייתא where he says that תרומה separated by mistake or on purpose still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. Just as you heard this from רבי יוסי, you heard it from רבי אליעזר. As it is taught: רבי אליעזר says, whether by mistake or on purpose, his תרומה is תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by bringing a source. In it, רבי אליעזר lets something done on purpose still count, with no fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of תרומה, רבי אליעזר does not penalize the person who acted on purpose: his separation still works. That shows he generally does not impose a קנס for acting on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Done by mistake, without knowing
Done on purpose, knowingly
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Just as

phrases.english: Yes

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: Just as you heard it from Rabbi Yosei
you heard it from Rabbi Eliezer
as it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer says
whether by mistake or on purpose
his תרומה is תרומה

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, כִּי הֵיכִי דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing a source that shows the sage's general approach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe רבי אליעזר penalizes someone who acted on purpose
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר does not penalize, as shown in the case of תרומה

steps.title: Maybe תרומה is different because it is lighter than קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof. רבי אליעזר may be lenient only with תרומה, which is a lighter matter, and not with קדשים, which are stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, you heard רבי אליעזר say this about תרומה, which is lenient. But did you hear him say it about קדשים, which are strict?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 23. A rule about a light area may not carry over to a strict one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being lenient about תרומה does not mean being lenient about offerings. With holier things, the חכמים might want to fine someone who acted on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Lenient, of lighter weight
Consecrated items, such as offerings
Stricter, more severe

phrases.english: Say that you heard it from Rabbi Eliezer
regarding תרומה, which is lenient
regarding קדשים, which are strict — did you hear it from him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בִּתְרוּמָה דְּקִילָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the תרומה ruling to show what רבי אליעזר holds about קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומה is lighter than קדשים, so leniency there may not carry over

steps.title: Who else could the lenient ברייתא belong to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if רבי אליעזר did not hold this for קדשים, there would be no one to assign the lenient ברייתא to. So it must be his.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, to whom will you assign this ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by process of elimination. The lenient ברייתא has to belong to someone, and only רבי אליעזר fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lenient ברייתא cannot be רבי יוסי's, since he holds the ציץ does not work for eaten parts (Steps 6 and 20). It cannot be the רבנן's, since they penalize someone who acted on purpose (Step 4). That leaves רבי אליעזר, so the ruling that there is no fine for acting on purpose must be his, even for קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
On whom will you place it? To whom can you assign this source?

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, the lenient ברייתא is רבי אליעזר. He holds that the ציץ makes the eaten parts acceptable, and that there is no fine even for acting on purpose. The strict ברייתא is the רבנן.

phrases.english: If so
to whom will you assign this one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24 and confirms רב חסדא's answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Process of elimination: no other author is possible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר may be strict about acting on purpose with קדשים
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא must be רבי אליעזר's, so he does not penalize even with קדשים

steps.title: רבינא: the impurity versus the sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: רבינא settles the contradiction differently. How the blood became impure does not matter, but sprinkling it on purpose while knowing it is impure makes the offering not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: about its impurity, whether it happened by mistake or on purpose, the offering is accepted. About its sprinkling, if done by mistake it is accepted, and if done on purpose it is not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a whole new answer. He says the two ברייתות are talking about two different acts, so they do not argue at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lenient ברייתא is about how the blood became impure. That can be by mistake or on purpose, and the offering is accepted either way. The strict ברייתא is about the sprinkling. If the כהן knew the blood was impure and sprinkled it anyway, the offering is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Its becoming impure
Its sprinkling (the blood on the מזבח)
It was accepted (the offering works)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two acts. "On purpose" in the impurity part means making the blood impure on purpose. "On purpose" in the sprinkling part means sprinkling blood the כהן knew was impure. Only the second one ruins the offering.
steps.whatToRemember: So far there are two standing answers to the contradiction (רב שילא will add another). רב חסדא says the ברייתות follow two different opinions (רבי אליעזר and the רבנן). רבינא says they cover two different acts: becoming impure, which is always accepted, and sprinkling, which is not accepted if done on purpose.

phrases.english: Ravina said
Its impurity
whether by mistake or on purpose — it is accepted
Its sprinkling: by mistake — it is accepted
on purpose — it is not accepted

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: טוּמְאָתוֹ, בֵּין בְּשׁוֹגֵג בֵּין בְּמֵזִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different way to settle the contradiction instead of רב חסדא's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each ברייתא is about a different act
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות are talking about the same thing, so they contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Becoming impure is always accepted, but sprinkling on purpose is not accepted

steps.title: רב שילא's opposite way of settling the contradiction
steps.stepSummary: רב שילא says the opposite of רבינא. Sprinkling the blood by mistake or on purpose is accepted. But if the blood became impure on purpose, it is not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב שילא said: As for its sprinkling, whether by mistake or on purpose, it is accepted. As for its becoming impure, if by mistake it is accepted, but if on purpose it is not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer to the contradiction, from רב שילא. His answer is the mirror image of רבינא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא said that how the blood became impure does not matter, and only sprinkling it on purpose ruins it. רב שילא flips this. How it was sprinkled does not matter, but making the blood impure on purpose means the ציץ does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling or throwing the blood of an offering on the מזבח
Ritual impurity
By mistake, without knowing
On purpose, knowingly
The offering is accepted (it counts)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two answers. רבינא: the sprinkling on purpose is the problem. רב שילא: the impurity on purpose is the problem.

phrases.english: And רב שילא said:
Its sprinkling, whether by mistake or on purpose —
it is accepted.
Its becoming impure: if by mistake, it is accepted;
if on purpose, it is not accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite answer to רבינא's answer in Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the 'on purpose' that matters is the impurity, not the sprinkling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One ברייתא says on purpose is accepted and another says it is not, so they seem to argue.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא that accepts 'on purpose' is talking about the sprinkling. The one that rejects 'on purpose' is talking about making the blood impure.

steps.title: How רב שילא reads the ברייתא that accepts impurity on purpose
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא said the blood is accepted when it became impure by mistake or on purpose. רב שילא reads it to mean: it became impure by mistake, and then it was sprinkled by mistake or on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב שילא, the ברייתא teaches that the blood 'became impure, whether by mistake or on purpose.' This is what it means: it became impure by mistake, and he sprinkled it, whether by mistake or on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא deals with a ברייתא that seems to go against רב שילא. It shows that the words 'by mistake or on purpose' in that ברייתא really refer to the sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to say that even blood made impure on purpose is accepted, which goes against רב שילא. The גמרא explains that the ברייתא is short on words. The impurity was by mistake, and 'by mistake or on purpose' describes the sprinkling, which רב שילא agrees does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means: the גמרא explains the real meaning of a source
It became impure
He sprinkled it (the blood)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב שילא, the ציץ helps when the blood became impure by mistake, no matter how it was sprinkled. If the blood was made impure on purpose, it is not accepted.

phrases.english: And according to רב שילא, that which is taught:
"that became impure, whether by mistake or on purpose" —
this is what it means:
it became impure by mistake, and he sprinkled it,
whether by mistake or on purpose.
phrases.notes: Now these words describe the sprinkling, not the impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב שילא's answer from Step 27 by explaining a ברייתא that seemed to go against it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: the ברייתא leaves out words, and 'whether by mistake or on purpose' refers to the sprinkling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seems to say that blood made impure on purpose is also accepted, which goes against רב שילא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means the impurity was by mistake, and only the sprinkling could be by mistake or on purpose.
